strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets a scheduled headless caller recover after an interrupted response even when route or closure child drives committed but the outer journey execution checkpoint was not advanced.
Keeps the Golden Journey moving through existing task and run-control boundaries while reconciling committed child-drive evidence before selecting any new boundary.
Reuses already committed Mode Pack fetch, provenance, approval, replacement, and closure checkpoints instead of asking the caller to reconstruct route envelopes.

Validates recovered child checkpoints against journey identity, drive identity, route kind, start sequence, source fingerprints, and closure replacement evidence before treating a boundary as complete.
Repairs compact execution checkpoint state from bounded checkpoint metadata, avoiding raw context or payload reconstruction after restart.
Returns bounded execution metadata for reconciled boundaries, replay state, completion state, and next action.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, persistent ledger evidence, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive now scans committed Golden Journey child drive checkpoints for fetch, provenance, approval, replacement, and closure before executing a new boundary, then advances or completes the outer execution checkpoint from validated persisted evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.7 recovered the outer execution checkpoint and admission boundary, but if a process died after a route or closure child drive committed and before the outer execution checkpoint advanced, the next caller could stall or duplicate boundary choreography.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled headless controller would still need external knowledge of half-committed route and closure drives to recover safely after an interrupted response.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.5 replacement, M50.6 closure, and M50.7 execution admission/checkpointing because it reconciles already committed child-drive evidence into the outer execution checkpoint after interruption.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase strengthens existing headless.run.drive journey_execution behavior without adding an RPC.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds recovery behavior and bounded checkpoint evidence, not a report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust validates and replays committed route and closure child checkpoints, advances the execution checkpoint for each recovered boundary, completes the task when recovering closure, and appends HeadlessJourneyExecuted idempotently.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless caller can resubmit the same authorized execution after a crash and let the runtime reconcile committed boundary evidence before doing any new work.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the last M50 restart-safety gap by making the Golden Journey execution path recover through all committed boundaries rather than only admission.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.8 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime Golden Journey reconciliation phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive journey_execution recovers committed admission, route, and closure child drive checkpoints before executing any new boundary
route recovery validates session id, child drive id, expected start sequence, journey/task/run/session identity, route kind, source checkpoint fingerprint, and resume fingerprint
closure recovery validates replacement boundary evidence, child drive identity, replacement resume fingerprint, closure metadata, and records task completion plus HeadlessJourneyExecuted idempotently
outer execution checkpoints advance from recovered bounded child-drive metadata and complete when close_journey is recovered
recovery does not require caller-supplied journey_route_resume, journey_closure, or explicit Mode Pack target envelopes on the journey_execution path
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, broad runtime modularization, new RPC, or VSIX-owned policy is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_execution_recovers_committed_route_and_closure_checkpoints covers recovery from committed route and closure child-drive checkpoints without a pre-existing outer execution checkpoint.
Existing Rust behavior tests for journey_execution admission replay and admission checkpoint recovery remain passing.
cargo check -p brownie-runtime validates the runtime/store/protocol integration for the reconciliation path.

accepted_capability: Runtime-owned Golden Journey boundary checkpoint reconciliation through existing headless.run.drive journey_execution
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_journey_execution_recovers_committed_route_and_closure_checkpoints -- --nocapture validates route and closure checkpoint reconciliation.
cargo check -p brownie-runtime validates the Rust protocol, store, and runtime integration for the recovery helpers.
pnpm guard:phase-value and pnpm guard:product-completion validate the phase-value and product-completion gates.
safety_boundary: Reconciliation runs only inside authorized journey_execution on existing headless.run.drive.
Recovered child drive checkpoints must match the persisted journey identity, child drive id, start sequence, route kind, and SHA-256 source/resume fingerprints.
Closure recovery requires a recovered replacement boundary and validates replacement drive/resume evidence before marking the task complete or appending HeadlessJourneyExecuted.

RPC and ledger evidence remains bounded to ids, enum values, hashes, fingerprints, counts, replay state, completion state, and next action; raw provenance material, Mode Pack payloads, prompts, provider responses, file content, command output, environment values, paths, and secrets are not returned or ledgered.
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary wrapper
No generic scheduler, daemon, background worker, all-route workflow engine, or VSIX-owned policy
No automatic apply, provider, parent-join, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No behavior-preserving runtime-wide lib.rs modularization mixed into this product PR
rejected_alternatives: Adding a separate recovery inspection RPC was rejected because the existing journey_execution path must own reconciliation before any new boundary side effect.
Asking the caller to replay per-boundary route envelopes was rejected because it preserves caller-side choreography and does not improve headless restart autonomy.
Returning an execution preview was rejected because the phase must mutate persisted execution checkpoint state from committed child-drive evidence.
technical_debt: crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be modularized later by cohesive low-dependency domains in independently buildable PRs.
The Golden Journey route chain remains explicitly bounded to the supported Mode Pack fetch, provenance, approval, replacement, and closure boundaries.
next_capability_rationale: M50 can move to milestone closeout after review because runtime-owned execution can now recover through committed admission, route, replacement, and closure boundaries.
